verbalization: Taxifolin 3-O-beta-D-xylopyranoside is proposed to interact with Tyrosine--tRNA ligase, a protein involved in the translation of mRNA into proteins. This interaction is supported by a final score of 0.5002, indicating a plausible but not certain mechanistic link. The target of Tyrosine--tRNA ligase, (3S,4aS,6aR,6bS,8aS,12aS,14aS,14bR)-3-hydroxy-8a-(hydroxymethyl)-4,4,6a,6b,11,11,14b-heptamethyl-3,4a,5,6,7,8,9,10,12,12a,14,14a-dodecahydro-2H-picen-1-one, is directly linked to SCCH-26, a cell line that is often used in cancer research. The evidence suggests that Taxifolin 3-O-beta-D-xylopyranoside may modulate the activity of Tyrosine--tRNA ligase, potentially influencing the survival and proliferation of SCCH-26 cells. The mechanism is supported by the presence of a binding IC50, though the exact nature of the interaction remains to be fully elucidated. The relationship between Taxifolin 3-O-beta-D-xylopyranoside and SCCH-26 is thus plausible, but further experimental validation is required to confirm the therapeutic potential.
